ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two similar triangles, placed separately on the left and right; both triangles protrude to the left, and both have a vertical side on the right. Mark the vertices of the left triangle according to the method as A=left pointed point, B=upper-right point, C=lower-right point; the vertices of the right triangle as D=left pointed point, E=upper-right point, F=lower-right point. Reasoning: According to the image proportions, if connecting from the left pointed point A of the left triangle to any vertex D, E, F of the right triangle, the straight line will enter the interior angle region of the left triangle from A, therefore A-D, A-E, A-F will all pass through the left triangle and are not qualified. If connecting from B or C to vertices of the right triangle, these lines will not enter the interior of the left triangle at the left triangle, so only the right triangle needs to be checked again. For the right triangle, when BD and CD connect to the left pointed point D, they will not enter the interior of the right triangle, so they are valid; BE also avoids the two triangles, while CE will enter the interior of the right triangle; CF avoids the two triangles, while BF will enter the interior of the right triangle. Therefore the valid choices are BD, BE, CD, CF, a total of 4 kinds.

raw_record.question_text: The diagram (which is drawn to scale) shows two triangles. In how many ways can you choose two vertices, one in each triangle, so that the straight line through the two vertices does not cross either triangle?

method.method_draft: Label the left triangle's vertices as A = left point, B = upper-right point, C = lower-right point, and the right triangle's vertices as D = left point, E = upper-right point, F = lower-right point. From the scaled image, note that both triangles point left, with the vertical side on the right. For each possible pair, use the local angle test: a line through a chosen vertex crosses that triangle if, at that vertex, the line goes into the interior angle of the triangle. At A, any line to D, E, or F goes into the interior of the left triangle, so all A-pairs are invalid. From B and C, the lines to the right triangle do not enter the left triangle, so test them against the right triangle. For the right triangle, lines to D from B or C avoid the right triangle, so BD and CD are valid. The horizontal-ish top line BE avoids both triangles, while CE enters the right triangle; similarly CF avoids both triangles, while BF enters the right triangle. Thus the valid pairs are BD, BE, CD, and CF, giving 4 ways.

method.method_draft: Treat each triangle as a convex obstacle. A valid line through one vertex of each triangle must be a common supporting line: it may touch each triangle at the chosen vertex but must leave the interior of each triangle entirely on one side of the line. From the drawing, identify the common support lines determined by pairs of vertices. There is an upper external support through the two upper-right vertices, BE, and a lower external support through the two lower-right vertices, CF. There are also two inner support lines across the gap: one from the upper-right vertex of the left triangle to the left vertex of the right triangle, BD, and one from the lower-right vertex of the left triangle to the left vertex of the right triangle, CD. No line using the leftmost vertex of the left triangle is supporting, because it goes into that triangle; the remaining cross-pairs such as BF and CE cut through the right triangle. Therefore there are 4 supporting vertex-pair lines.
